ai.description: This 4–6 cm frog is brown with a distinct black lateral stripe extending from the snout through the eye to the flank. It features long, slender limbs and a pointed snout with a white upper lip.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Hylarana nigrovittata* is the distinct, broad black lateral stripe that extends from the snout through the eye to the groin, bordered by a white lip.
ai.habitat: The Black-striped Frog inhabits moist evergreen and deciduous forests, typically found near streams or pools at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Black-striped Frog is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for small insects and invertebrates along the damp forest floor and near stream banks after dark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana nigrovittata* breeds during the monsoon season, laying eggs in small, gelatinous clutches attached to submerged vegetation in stagnant or slow-moving water.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Black-striped Frog occurs in Northeast India, primarily in Assam and Mizoram, inhabiting low-elevation forests and wetlands within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
ai.callDescription: The Black-striped Frog emits a series of rapid, high-pitched "chuck" notes, typically heard near small streams or forest pools within its humid habitat.
